question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word.

My teacher is very diligent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Idle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diligent" means hardworking, careful and showing steady effort in one's work. Its antonym is "Idle", meaning lazy, inactive and not working. (परिश्रमी का विलोम — आलसी/निठल्ला)

◦ Example: A diligent student studies every day, while an idle one wastes time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Skilful" (having skill) and Option 3 "Hardworking" are synonyms, not antonyms, of diligent.

• Option 4 "Kind" (gentle, caring) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diligent: industrious, hardworking, assiduous, painstaking, conscientious. Antonyms: idle, lazy, negligent, careless.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Don't be such an ________; we have plenty of time to complete the task.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. eager beaver.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "eager beaver" means a person who is very enthusiastic and works extremely hard, often too keenly. It fits the sense of being told to relax as there is plenty of time. (अति उत्साही व्यक्ति)

◦ Correct: Don't be such an eager beaver; we have plenty of time to complete the task.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eat crow" (to admit one was wrong), Option 2 "easy money" (money earned with little effort) and Option 4 "elephant in the room" (an obvious problem everyone avoids discussing) do not fit the context.

NOTE

• "Eager beaver" is used, sometimes disapprovingly, for someone excessively willing or industrious. The grammatical clue "an" before the blank signals a noun phrase beginning with a vowel sound (eager).

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: She usually walks her dog in the park every morning.
option_2: The train leaves the station at 8:00 a.m. every day.
option_3: They play chess together on weekends.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He don't like spicy food.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the third person singular subject "He", the correct auxiliary is "does not (doesn't)", not "don't". So the sentence should be "He doesn't like spicy food."

◦ Correct: He does not (doesn't) like spicy food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are grammatically correct and use the simple present tense properly (walks / leaves / play).

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement in the simple present: I/you/we/they → do/don't; he/she/it → does/doesn't. "He don't" is a common non-standard error.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Scince explores and explains the natural world through observation and experimentation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. science.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "science", meaning the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experiment. (विज्ञान)

◦ Spelling key: S-C-I-E-N-C-E (remember "C" before "I" — sci-ence).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspellings: "sience", "sceince" and "scinece" all jumble the letters "i-e" and "c".

NOTE

• "Science" follows the pattern where "sc" is followed by "ience". Related words: scientist, scientific, conscience (with the "sci" cluster).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Congenial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pleasant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Congenial" means friendly, agreeable and pleasant; suited to one's taste. Its closest synonym is "pleasant". (सुखद / अनुकूल)

◦ Example: We spent the evening in congenial/pleasant company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Trivial" (unimportant), Option 3 "Ignorant" (lacking knowledge) and Option 4 "Ethical" (morally right) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of congenial: pleasant, agreeable, amiable, friendly, sympathetic. Antonyms: disagreeable, unpleasant, hostile.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Gandhi's ways of life, if followed in their entirety, will aid us in the creation of a society of peace and _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. harmony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harmony" means peaceful agreement and a state of being in accord. It pairs naturally with "peace" to describe an ideal society. (सामंजस्य / सद्भाव)

◦ Correct: ... will aid us in the creation of a society of peace and harmony.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cacophony" (a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds), Option 2 "agitation" (disturbance/unrest) and Option 4 "discord" (disagreement/conflict) all carry a negative sense opposite to "peace".

NOTE

• Synonyms of harmony: accord, concord, unity, peace. Antonyms: discord, conflict, disharmony, cacophony.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

It is a fact that / girls' hair is usually / long than the boys' hair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. long than the boys' hair.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "long" is "longer", so the segment should be "longer than the boys' hair".

◦ Correct: It is a fact that girls' hair is usually longer than the boys' hair.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "It is a fact that" and "girls' hair is usually" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Short adjectives form the comparative by adding "-er ... than" (long → longer than; tall → taller than). Never use the positive degree ("long") with "than".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Abundant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ample.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abundant" means existing in large quantities; plentiful and more than enough. Its closest synonym is "ample". (प्रचुर / भरपूर)

◦ Example: The region has an abundant/ample supply of water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Elusive" (hard to find/catch), Option 3 "Skimpy" (scanty, too little) and Option 4 "Rare" (uncommon) are antonyms or unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of abundant: ample, plentiful, copious, profuse, bountiful. Antonyms: scarce, scanty, sparse, meagre.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

When I was studying Economics in Delhi University, Ritu was senior than me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. senior than me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Senior" is a Latin comparative and is followed by the preposition "to", not "than". So it should be "senior to me".

◦ Correct: ... Ritu was senior to me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other segments ("When I was studying Economics", "in Delhi University", "Ritu was") are correct.

NOTE

• Latin comparatives take "to", not "than": senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, prior to, preferable to.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Perseverence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perseverence" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "perseverance", meaning persistence and steady effort in spite of difficulties. (दृढ़ता / लगन)

◦ Spelling key: PER + SEVER + ANCE (ends in "-ance", not "-ence").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Camouflage" (disguise/concealment), "Exaggerate" (to overstate) and "Connoisseur" (an expert judge in matters of taste) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Remember: perseverance (noun) and persevere (verb). Do not confuse the "-ance"/"-ence" endings — perseverance, appearance vs. difference, patience.

question:
Based on the context of the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

After spending hours working non-stop on the project, the team decided to ___________ and go home.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. call it a day.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "call it a day" means to stop working (for the day) and finish an activity. After working for hours, the team decided to stop and go home. (काम बंद करना / दिन का काम समाप्त करना)

◦ Correct: ... the team decided to call it a day and go home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "run out of steam" (to lose energy/momentum), Option 2 "take it easy" (to relax) and Option 3 "hit the books" (to study hard) do not fit as neatly with "and go home".

NOTE

• "Call it a day" (or "call it a night") signals the end of work. Related: "wrap up", "knock off", "wind up".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Elevation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Demotion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Elevation" means the act of raising to a higher position or rank. Its antonym is "Demotion", meaning a reduction to a lower rank or position. (उन्नयन का विलोम — पदावनति)

◦ Example: A promotion/elevation raises one's rank, while a demotion lowers it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Promotion" is a synonym of elevation.

• Options 3 "Creation" and 4 "Presentation" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of elevation: promotion, advancement, upgrading, rise. Antonyms: demotion, degradation, lowering.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

In an _____(endeavour) to improve the environment of their society, they planted many trees surrounding the parking area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. aim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Endeavour" means an earnest attempt or effort to achieve something. The closest synonym here is "aim" (a purpose or intention/effort). (प्रयास / लक्ष्य)

◦ Correct: In an aim to improve the environment of their society, they planted many trees ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "axiom" (a self-evident truth), Option 3 "ecstasy" (intense joy) and Option 4 "epitome" (a perfect example) do not match "endeavour".

NOTE

• Synonyms of endeavour: attempt, effort, aim, try, undertaking. As a verb, "endeavour to" = to try hard to do something.

question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Ramesh is not stronger than Mahesh.
option_1: Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh.
option_3: Ramesh is as strong than Mahesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ramesh is not stronger than Mahesh" (comparative) means Mahesh is at least equal to Ramesh in strength. In the positive degree, a negative comparative "not ... -er than" becomes "as ... as": "Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh."

◦ Correct transformation: Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "strongest than" and Option 3 "as strong than" mix degrees wrongly.

• Option 4 keeps the comparative and reverses the meaning.

NOTE

• Degree change rule: "A is not stronger than B" (comparative) ⇄ "A is as strong as B" (positive). The positive degree uses "as + adjective + as".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The company's success is attributed to its __________ business strategies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. innovative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Innovative" means featuring new methods, original and creative in thinking. Success is naturally attributed to fresh, creative strategies. (नवोन्मेषी / नवाचारी)

◦ Correct: The company's success is attributed to its innovative business strategies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "worst", Option 2 "downtrodden" (oppressed) and Option 3 "mundane" (dull, ordinary) carry negative or unfitting senses that would not explain success.

NOTE

• Synonyms of innovative: inventive, original, creative, groundbreaking, pioneering. Antonyms: conventional, unoriginal, mundane.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Swati came here with the intent of insulting me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. to insult me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "intent", the natural and idiomatic construction is "the intent to + verb" (an infinitive of purpose). So "with the intent to insult me" is correct.

◦ Correct: Swati came here with the intent to insult me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "off insulting", "for insulting" and "from insulting" are all unidiomatic here. While "intention of insulting" can be used, "intent to insult" is the standard collocation.

NOTE

• "Intent" collocates with the infinitive: "with intent to deceive/harm/insult". Compare "intention of + -ing" (intention of leaving).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Occassionaly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Occassionaly" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "occasionally", meaning sometimes; now and then. (कभी-कभी)

◦ Spelling key: OC + CA + SION + ALLY — one "s", double "l" (occasion → occasionally).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Synopsis" (a summary), "Obliterate" (to destroy completely) and "Pursuit" (the act of chasing/seeking) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Common confusion: "occasion" has double "c" and single "s"; the adverb "occasionally" ends in "-ally" (double "l"). Do not double the "s".

question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Neha's house is far from the city than everyone else's.
option_2: more far from the city to
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. farther from the city than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Than" requires the comparative degree. For physical/literal distance, the correct comparative of "far" is "farther". So "farther from the city than everyone else's".

◦ Correct: Neha's house is farther from the city than everyone else's.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "further" is usually preferred for figurative/abstract extent (further information), though it is sometimes interchangeable; for literal distance "farther" is more precise.

• Options 2 "more far" (double comparative) and 4 "far ... to" (no comparative, wrong preposition) are incorrect.

NOTE

• Distinction: farther/farthest for physical distance; further/furthest for additional degree or extent. Both are comparatives of "far" and take "than".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Chocolate can be ______ without milk; mix cocoa butter, sugar and a puree of fermented, roasted cocoa beans, and you _______ a perfectly respectable dark chocolate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. made; have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank is in a passive construction ("Chocolate can be ______"), which needs the past participle "made" (can be made).

• The second blank has the subject "you", which takes the plural verb "have" (you have a perfectly respectable dark chocolate).

◦ Correct: Chocolate can be made without milk; ... and you have a perfectly respectable dark chocolate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "make" and "making" cannot follow "can be" (which needs V3 = made).

• "has" is wrong with "you"; it is used only with third person singular (he/she/it).

NOTE

• Passive: subject + be + past participle (can be made). Subject–verb agreement: I/you/we/they → have; he/she/it → has.

question:
Select the option that changes the degree of comparison in the given sentence from superlative to positive without changing the meaning of the sentence.

Kalpana Ahuja is the tallest girl in the colony.
option_1: Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja.
option_2: Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls of the colony.
option_3: No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja.
option_4: No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A superlative ("the tallest") is changed to the positive degree using the pattern "No other ... is as + positive adjective + as ...". So "the tallest girl" becomes "No other girl ... is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja."

◦ Correct: No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 changes the meaning (making her not the tallest).

• Options 2 and 3 wrongly use "tallest"/"taller" with "as ... as", which must take the positive form "tall".

NOTE

• Degree change: "X is the tallest" (superlative) = "No other ... is as tall as X" (positive) = "X is taller than all other ..." (comparative). The positive form uses "as tall as".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

That was a jolly story _____1_____ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking __2___ her basket down the middle of a street to the _____3_____ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed _____4_____ to her that the _____5_____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, "I'm going to walk where I like. We've got liberty now."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. which.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 1 needs a relative pronoun to connect "a jolly story" with "Arthur Ransome told". "which" correctly introduces the relative clause referring to the story (a thing). (संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम)

◦ Correct: That was a jolly story which Arthur Ransome told the other day ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "about" and Option 2 "off" are prepositions that do not link the clauses here.

• Option 4 "form" is a noun/verb and is contextually and grammatically wrong.

NOTE

• Use "which"/"that" as a relative pronoun for things and "who" for people. Here "story" is a thing, so "which" is apt.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

That was a jolly story _____1_____ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking __2___ her basket down the middle of a street to the _____3_____ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed _____4_____ to her that the _____5_____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, "I'm going to walk where I like. We've got liberty now."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 2 describes the old lady carrying her basket. "walking with her basket" is the natural, idiomatic expression (carrying it along). (अपनी टोकरी के साथ)

◦ Correct: A stout old lady was walking with her basket down the middle of a street ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "beside" (next to), Option 2 "in" and Option 3 "at" do not fit the sense of carrying the basket while walking.

NOTE

• "With" indicates accompaniment or possession — walking with a basket, a stick, a dog. It best conveys that she carried her basket.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

That was a jolly story _____1_____ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking __2___ her basket down the middle of a street to the _____3_____ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed _____4_____ to her that the _____5_____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, "I'm going to walk where I like. We've got liberty now."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. great.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 3 needs an adjective to describe the "confusion of the traffic". "great" (meaning large in degree/considerable) fits — "the great confusion of the traffic". (बहुत अधिक / भारी)

◦ Correct: ... down the middle of a street to the great confusion of the traffic ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "greet" (to welcome) is a verb, Option 2 "grate" (to shred / a fireplace frame) and Option 4 "garret" (an attic room) are unrelated homophones/near-homophones.

NOTE

• These options are close in spelling/sound (greet, grate, great, garret) — a spelling-cum-context trap. Only "great" is an adjective meaning large/considerable that suits "confusion".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

That was a jolly story _____1_____ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking __2___ her basket down the middle of a street to the _____3_____ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed _____4_____ to her that the _____5_____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, "I'm going to walk where I like. We've got liberty now."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "point out" means to draw attention to / indicate something. So "It was pointed out to her that the pavement was the place for foot passengers." (बताया गया / इंगित किया गया)

◦ Correct: It was pointed out to her that the pavement was the place for the foot passengers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "pointed in", "pointed by" and "pointed so" are not correct phrasal expressions in this context.

NOTE

• "Point out" = to mention or make someone notice a fact. Related phrasal verbs: point to, point at (to indicate direction).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

That was a jolly story _____1_____ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking __2___ her basket down the middle of a street to the _____3_____ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed _____4_____ to her that the _____5_____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, "I'm going to walk where I like. We've got liberty now."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. pavement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 5 refers to the proper place for "the foot passengers" (pedestrians). That place is the "pavement" (British English for footpath/sidewalk). She was walking in the middle of the street instead of on the pavement. (फुटपाथ)

◦ Correct: ... that the pavement was the place for the foot passengers ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "road" is where vehicles move (she was wrongly there), Option 3 "market" and Option 4 "bay" do not fit "the place for foot passengers".

NOTE

• In British English, "pavement" = the raised path for pedestrians beside a road; in American English this is called the "sidewalk".

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 79.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 79 of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Parliament for the Union consisting of the President and the two Houses — the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha). (अनुच्छेद 79)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 80 — composition of the Rajya Sabha; Article 81 — composition of the Lok Sabha.

• Although the President is not a member of either House, the President is an integral part of Parliament.

NOTE

• Related Articles: Article 74 (Council of Ministers to aid the President), Article 84 (qualification for membership of Parliament — minimum age 25 for Lok Sabha, 30 for Rajya Sabha).

question: Which edition of the Santosh Trophy event did Karnataka win in the 2022-23 season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 76th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Karnataka won the 76th edition of the Santosh Trophy in the 2022-23 season, defeating Meghalaya in the final (held partly in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh). (76वां संतोष ट्रॉफी — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy is a premier national football knockout competition in India among States and government institutions, first held in 1941.

• It is named after Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary, the Maharaja of Santosh (in present-day Bangladesh).

NOTE

• Football in India is governed by the All India Football Federation (AIFF). West Bengal has won the Santosh Trophy the most number of times.

question: Ortho-sulphobenzimide is one of the artificial sweeteners. It is also known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is saccharin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ortho-sulphobenzimide is the chemical name of "saccharin", one of the earliest artificial sweeteners. It is about 550 times sweeter than cane sugar (sucrose) and provides no calories. (सैकरीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Saccharin is not metabolised by the body, so it is used by diabetics and in low-calorie foods.

• Other artificial sweeteners: aspartame, sucralose, alitame — differing in sweetness and stability on heating.

NOTE

• Aspartame is about 100 times sweeter than sugar but is unstable at cooking temperatures; sucralose is stable at cooking temperature and is widely used in baked goods.

question: Which of the following is NOT an iron-ore producing belt of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bilaspur-Panipat belt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bilaspur-Panipat belt" is NOT an iron-ore producing belt of India. The major iron-ore belts of India are the Odisha-Jharkhand belt, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt, Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt, and the Maharashtra-Goa belt. (बिलासपुर-पानीपत — लौह अयस्क बेल्ट नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Odisha-Jharkhand belt — high-grade haematite ore (Mayurbhanj, Kendujhar, Singhbhum).

• Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt (Chhattisgarh–Maharashtra) — famous Bailadila mines.

• Maharashtra-Goa belt — ore of not very high quality, largely exported.

NOTE

• India's iron ores are mainly haematite and magnetite. India is one of the leading producers and exporters of iron ore in the world.

question: Which of the following was the capital of the Pallava Dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanchipuram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kanchipuram" (in present-day Tamil Nadu) was the capital of the Pallava Dynasty. The Pallavas ruled parts of South India between roughly the 3rd and 9th centuries CE. (कांचीपुरम — पल्लव राजधानी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Pallavas were great patrons of art and architecture; the Shore Temple and the Rathas (monolithic temples) at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) and the Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram are their creations.

• Famous Pallava rulers include Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla).

NOTE

• Aihole and Badami were centres of the Chalukyas of Badami; Madurai was the capital of the Pandyas. Kanchipuram is also known as a "city of a thousand temples".

question: Hareli festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hareli" is an important agricultural festival celebrated in Chhattisgarh. It marks the beginning of the monsoon/cropping season, when farmers worship their farm equipment and cattle and pray for a good harvest. (हरेली — छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Hareli" comes from the word "hariyali" (greenery). It is considered the first festival of the year in Chhattisgarh, celebrated in the month of Sawan (Shravan).

• Other festivals of Chhattisgarh: Bastar Dussehra, Madai, Pola, Teej.

NOTE

• Farming/harvest festivals across India: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Bihu (Assam), Baisakhi (Punjab), Onam (Kerala), Hareli (Chhattisgarh).

question: Kamalini Asthana is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kamalini Asthana is a renowned exponent of the Kathak classical dance form. Along with Nalini Asthana, she belongs to the Lucknow gharana of Kathak. (कथक — कमलिनी अस्थाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), noted for intricate footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling. Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Kathak was patronised by both Hindu (temple) and Mughal (court) traditions.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: Which of the following is referred to as 'Near Money'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National savings deposits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Near money" refers to highly liquid financial assets that are not money themselves but can be quickly converted into cash, such as National savings deposits, time/fixed deposits, treasury bills and bonds. (निकट मुद्रा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Coins and currency notes are actual (legal-tender) money; bank money (demand deposits) is directly usable for payments.

• Near money assets earn interest and are one step away from being spent, but cannot be used directly as a medium of exchange.

NOTE

• Measures of money supply: M1 (narrow money) = currency + demand deposits; near-money assets like time deposits are included in the broader measures (M3).

question: ICC Women's T-20 Cricket World Cup is a/an ________ event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is biennial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Women's T20 World Cup is a "biennial" event, i.e., it is held once every two years. (द्विवार्षिक — प्रत्येक दो वर्ष में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The first ICC Women's T20 World Cup was held in 2009 (won by England). Australia is the most successful team in the tournament.

• "Biennial" = every two years; "biannual" = twice a year — do not confuse the two.

NOTE

• Meanings: quarterly (every 3 months), annual (every year), biennial (every 2 years), triennial (every 3 years).

question: Who among the following formed a group of non-violent revolutionaries, the Khudai Khidmatgars (known as Red Shirts)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (popularly called "Frontier Gandhi" or "Badshah Khan") founded the Khudai Khidmatgars ("Servants of God"), a non-violent movement in the North-West Frontier Province. They were also known as the "Red Shirts (Surkh Posh)" because of their red-coloured uniforms. (खुदाई खिदमतगार — खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Khudai Khidmatgars supported the Indian National Congress and participated actively in the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930).

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was later awarded the Bharat Ratna (1987) — the first non-Indian citizen to receive it.

NOTE

• He strongly opposed the Partition of India in 1947, famously saying the Pashtuns had been "thrown to the wolves".

question: The founders of Vijayanagar empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya were the ministers of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kampili.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harihara and Bukka Raya, the founders of the Vijayanagara Empire (1336), were originally ministers/treasury officers in the kingdom of Kampili before founding their own empire. (कंपिली — हरिहर और बुक्का)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• They founded the Vijayanagara Empire and the Sangama dynasty, with their capital at Hampi on the banks of the Tungabhadra river.

• They were guided by the sage Vidyaranya, and the city was named Vijayanagara ("City of Victory").

NOTE

• The four dynasties that ruled Vijayanagara: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu. Its greatest ruler was Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty).

question: In May 2023, which Chief Minister was honoured with the Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar award for creating a fear-free state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yogi Adityanath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2023, Yogi Adityanath, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, was honoured with the "Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar Award" for creating a fear-free (crime-controlled) state. (योगी आदित्यनाथ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Yogi Adityanath became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 2017 and again in 2022.

• (Note: This "Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar Award" is a separate honour and should not be confused with the national Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.)

NOTE

• Uttar Pradesh is India's most populous state and sends the largest number of members (80) to the Lok Sabha.

question: Identify the group of states that is a part of Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (As of June 2022).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand were among the states covered under the Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA). The scheme covered six states — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Odisha. (उत्तर प्रदेश और झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan was launched on 20 June 2020 to provide employment and livelihood to migrant workers who returned to their villages during the COVID-19 lockdown.

• It was launched from Khagaria district, Bihar, and focused on the construction of durable rural infrastructure.

NOTE

• The scheme covered 116 districts across the six states, each having a large number of returnee migrant workers.

question:
Which of the following statements with reference to Padma Subrahmanyam is/are correct?
1) Padma Subrahmanyam is a famous Bharatanatyam dancer.
2) She received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.
3) She was also honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2, and 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three statements about Padma Subrahmanyam are correct:

◦ (1) She is a famous Bharatanatyam dancer and research scholar.

◦ (2) She has received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan (and later Padma Vibhushan).

◦ (3) She was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for dance. (पद्म सुब्रह्मण्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Padma Subrahmanyam is renowned for her research on the karanas described in Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and developed the concept of Bharata Nrityam.

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu; its major exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati and Yamini Krishnamurthy.

question: Which percussionist from Maharashtra received Padma Vibhushan 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zakir Hussain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain (from Maharashtra) was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2023. He is one of the most celebrated percussionists in the world. (उस्ताद ज़ाकिर हुसैन — पद्म विभूषण 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Zakir Hussain earlier received the Padma Shri (1988) and Padma Bhushan (2002), and he is a multiple Grammy Award winner.

• He is the son of the famous tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha.

NOTE

• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award of India (after the Bharat Ratna), given for exceptional and distinguished service.

question: Which of the following is an autobiography of Abul Kalam Azad, the first education minister of India?
option_1: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
solution_text:
The correct answer is India Wins Freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "India Wins Freedom" is the autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the first Education Minister of independent India. (इंडिया विन्स फ्रीडम — मौलाना अबुल कलाम आज़ाद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a senior Congress leader and freedom fighter; his birthday, 11 November, is celebrated as National Education Day in India.

• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1992.

NOTE

• Other books: The Story of My Experiments with Truth (M. K. Gandhi), My Country My Life (L. K. Advani), Long Walk to Freedom (Nelson Mandela).

question: What is the chemical formula for potassium permanganate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is KMnO4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The chemical formula of potassium permanganate is "KMnO₄". It is a dark purple crystalline solid and a strong oxidising agent. (पोटैशियम परमैंगनेट — KMnO₄)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In KMnO₄, the oxidation state of manganese (Mn) is +7.

• It is used as a disinfectant, water-purifying agent, and in titrations (potassium permanganate titrations / permanganometry).

NOTE

• Potassium permanganate is also known as "Condy's crystals". A dilute solution is used to treat skin infections and to purify drinking water.

question:
Which of the following statements about pteridophytes are correct?
Statements:
A. They include horsetails and ferns.
B. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders.
C. They are very advanced type of plants on earth, which evolved very recently.
D. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A, B and D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statements A, B and D about pteridophytes are correct:

◦ (A) They include horsetails and ferns.

◦ (B) They are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders.

◦ (D) They are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).

• Statement C is wrong — pteridophytes are not a very advanced or recently evolved group; they are among the earliest/primitive vascular plants. (टेरिडोफाइट्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pteridophytes (e.g., ferns, horsetails, club mosses) are seedless vascular plants (cryptogams) that reproduce through spores.

• They are sometimes called the "amphibians of the plant kingdom" as they need water for reproduction.

NOTE

• Plant kingdom classification: Thallophyta (algae), Bryophyta (mosses), Pteridophyta (ferns), Gymnosperms and Angiosperms. Pteridophytes are the first to have true roots, stems and leaves with vascular tissue.

question: In July 2023, the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) in Tirupathur district, Tamil Nadu, achieved a monumental achievement by constructing 1546 farm ponds in just 30 days, setting a new world record. This remarkable initiative was carried out under which government scheme?
option_1: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2023, the DRDA in Tirupathur district, Tamil Nadu, built 1546 farm ponds in 30 days — a world record — under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS). (मनरेगा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• MGNREGA (2005) guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development and is the world's largest work-guarantee programme.

NOTE

• Mission Amrit Sarovar aims to develop/rejuvenate 75 water bodies (Amrit Sarovars) in each district of India; Jal Jeevan Mission provides tap water to rural households.

question: Bokaro, Burnpur, Rourkela, etc., are famous for development of which of the following industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron and Steel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bokaro, Burnpur and Rourkela are famous centres of the Iron and Steel industry in India. They house major integrated steel plants. (लौह एवं इस्पात उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rourkela Steel Plant (Odisha) was set up with German collaboration; Bhilai (Chhattisgarh) with Russian (USSR) collaboration; Durgapur (West Bengal) with British collaboration.

• Bokaro Steel Plant (Jharkhand) was also set up with Russian help; Burnpur (IISCO) is in West Bengal.

NOTE

• These plants are located in the Chota Nagpur plateau region (mineral belt), which is rich in coal and iron ore, essential raw materials for steel-making. SAIL manages most of these plants.

question: By which of the following Amendments was the right to property removed from Part III of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 44th Amendment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights (Part III) and made it a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII. (44वां संविधान संशोधन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Earlier, the Right to Property was a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, both of which were repealed by the 44th Amendment.

• The 44th Amendment was enacted during the Morarji Desai (Janata Party) government to undo several changes made by the 42nd Amendment (the "Mini-Constitution").

NOTE

• After the amendment, no person can be deprived of property except by authority of law (Article 300A). It is now a constitutional/legal right, not a fundamental right.

question: Which state has the highest population in India as per the projected data of 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India, both as per the 2011 Census and the projected data for 2024. (उत्तर प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• As per the 2011 Census, Uttar Pradesh had a population of about 19.98 crore (200 million).

• It is followed by Maharashtra and Bihar in terms of population.

NOTE

• Uttar Pradesh sends the highest number of members to both the Lok Sabha (80) and the Rajya Sabha (31). Sikkim is the least populous state.

question: Divergent plate boundary is a boundary that occurs between two tectonic plates:
option_1: that are moving towards one another
option_2: where one plate slides beneath the other
option_3: that are sliding horizontally past each other
option_4: that are moving away from one another
solution_text:
The correct answer is that are moving away from one another.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "divergent (constructive) plate boundary" occurs between two tectonic plates that are "moving away from one another". Magma rises to fill the gap, creating new crust. (अपसारी प्लेट सीमा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• At divergent boundaries, features like mid-ocean ridges (e.g., the Mid-Atlantic Ridge) and rift valleys (e.g., the East African Rift) are formed.

• When plates move towards each other it is a convergent boundary; when they slide past each other it is a transform boundary.

NOTE

• The theory of Plate Tectonics explains the movement of the Earth's lithospheric plates. Sea-floor spreading is a result of divergent boundaries.

question: Which of the following pacts suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gandhi-Irwin Pact" (signed on 5 March 1931) led to the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Mahatma Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference in London. (गांधी-इरविन समझौता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Under the pact, the government agreed to release political prisoners (except those guilty of violence) and to allow coastal villagers to make salt for personal use.

• Lord Irwin was the Viceroy of India at the time; the pact is also called the Delhi Pact.

NOTE

• The Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Dandi/Salt March (1930). It was resumed later when the Round Table Conference failed and Gandhi was arrested.

question: Who discovered the Bharhut stupa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alexander Cunningham.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharhut Stupa (in Madhya Pradesh) was discovered by Alexander Cunningham in 1873. He is regarded as the "Father of Indian Archaeology". (भरहुत स्तूप — अलेक्जेंडर कनिंघम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Alexander Cunningham was the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), established in 1861.

• The Bharhut Stupa dates to the Shunga period (2nd century BCE) and is famous for its sculpted railings and gateways, many of which are now in the Indian Museum, Kolkata.

NOTE

• Other stupas: the Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh) built by Ashoka, and the Amaravati Stupa (Andhra Pradesh). Stupas are Buddhist monuments containing relics.
